reading.title: A static fire test
reading.text: Before a new rocket flies, engineers test its engines on the ground. This is called a static fire test. The rocket is held down by strong clamps, so it cannot move. The engines run for a few seconds while hundreds of sensors measure pressure, temperature and vibration. After the test, the team compares the data with the computer model. If the numbers match, the rocket is ready for the next step. If they do not match, engineers look for the reason before they continue. A short test on the ground is much cheaper than a failure in flight.

reading.title: Why composite specimens fail
reading.text: Carbon fiber reinforced polymers are widely used in aerospace structures because they combine high stiffness with low weight. However, their failure behavior is more complex than that of metals. In a standard tensile test, a flat specimen is loaded until it breaks, while strain gauges record its elongation. Unlike aluminum, which yields gradually, a composite laminate often fails with little warning. Damage usually begins as small cracks in the matrix, which then grow along the interfaces between plies. This process, known as delamination, can significantly reduce compressive strength even when the surface appears undamaged. For this reason, engineers combine mechanical tests with non-destructive inspection methods, such as ultrasonic scanning, to detect hidden damage before it becomes critical.
